deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is not Riemann's own work. It is the first page of a letter from Richard Dedekind to Heinrich Weber, written in March 1876, shortly after Dedekind's letter of 16 March 1876 on the previous folio. The two were then editing Riemann's 'Gesammelte mathematische Werke' (abbreviated 'R. g. m. W.'), printed by Teubner and first published in 1876.

What the page says, in order:
(1) Dedekind thanks Weber for a letter and a card that relieved his worry, after he had complained of hearing nothing.
(2) The supposed 'fourth' Abteilung (section) of the edition surprised him too. He had suspected a misunderstanding: in the clean proofs of sheets (Bogen) 1–26 the running mark 'R. g. m. W. I' had stayed on every sheet, although he had corrected it to II and III in sections II and III.
(3) He still has no second proof of the last sheet, 27. He would like one if the 'fourth' section is dropped and two more pages of the elliptic fragments go onto sheet 27.
(4) At Weber's request he has recomputed, 'exactly along Riemann's route', the formulas of the second fragment. These are the eight formulas in Riemann's posthumous fragment on the limiting cases of the elliptic modular functions (Werke, Fragment XXVIII), on the behaviour of log η(ω) as ω approaches rational points. He had dreaded the calculation, having already found at Christmas, with the first of the eight formulas, how laborious and delicate it is. It took him almost a week, and he no longer regrets it.
(5) He calls the pale manuscript 'schauderbar' (dreadful). Judging from the many deletions and side calculations, Riemann seems to have done the computation for the first time on that sheet. The sentence continues on the next folio, where Dedekind conjectures that Riemann used a slate and wrote down only the key steps.

The mathematical content Dedekind refers to appears on the following page, not here. That content is the identities with sums of (-1)^s E(ms/2n) and the sawtooth ((x)), the corrections to Riemann's final formulas, and the claim that the real parts disagree with his own log η formulas. This is the origin of Dedekind's 'Erläuterungen' to Fragment XXVIII and of the Dedekind sums s(m,n) and the η transformation law.

There is nothing on this page to reconstruct mathematically.

results.what: Historical/editorial information only: Dedekind reports recomputing, at Weber's request, the eight formulas of Riemann's second fragment on the limiting values of modular functions (log eta near rational points). He describes Riemann's manuscript as a first-draft computation with gaps.
results.modern_name: Context: Dedekind's commentary on Riemann's Fragment XXVIII (origin of Dedekind sums / transformation law of the Dedekind eta function)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (fragment, published posthumously 1876); Dedekind (Erläuterungen, 1876; Dedekind sums)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an editorial letter by Dedekind, not a Riemann computation, and contains no mathematics. Riemann's authorship of the limiting-case fragment and Dedekind's role in checking it and introducing Dedekind sums are well documented in the Werke and the Dedekind–Weber correspondence.
transcription_corrections: The page is a letter of Dedekind to Weber (continuation of the correspondence after the letter signed 'Braunschweig, 16 März 1876. R. Dedekind'), not a Riemann manuscript page.
'blaße' should be read as 'blasse' (pale), consistent with 'blassen Manuscriptes' on the next page.
'schau-derbar' could possibly be 'schau-derhaft'; the image reading is uncertain, but 'schauderbar' fits the visible letters.
Last line: the word before '-rechnungen' is struck out and 'Neben' is written above it, giving 'Nebenrechnungen'; the transcription's rendering is essentially correct.
'R. g. m. W. I' = 'Riemann's gesammelte mathematische Werke', the running sheet mark (Bogensignatur) for the edition.
